title: Hackers Stole Flock’s Camera Software, Revealing How the Company Tracks Cars and People
summary: Hackers physically removed a Flock ALPR camera and extracted its software and stored data, sharing it with 404 Media and WIRED. The joint analysis revealed the camera detects people as well as vehicles, generates massive image volumes, and sometimes misidentifies bumper stickers or patches as license plates. The article also notes that records from Alpharetta, GA's Flock cameras were accessible to more than 2,000 agencies nationwide.

key_quotes.quote: the joint analysis of the recovered data shows that software running on the device explicitly detects people as well as vehicles, license plates, and bicycles

In Alpharetta, Georgia, for example, WIRED found that records from the city's Flock cameras were accessible to more than 2,000 agencies, including police departments, colleges, airports, and even inexplicably the Office of Inspector General for the federal General Services Administration.
